main_text.p: 2 Triginta ÆOnas.) Breuius huius erroris hypothesis perstringam, quod & Epiphanius, & Theodoretus, & Tertullianus, & ante hos omnes Irenæus abundè, imò verò ad nauseam vsque referunt. Sex autè capita hîc habentur. Clemens autem Alexandrinus vbique Basilidem & Valentinum in dogmate coniungit.

1 Continet fabulosam de triginta ÆOnum tanquam deorum generatione narrationem, vbi nascentes & nubentes, & generantes sunt, AEones, inquit Tertullianus. Illæ autè nugæ de Hesiodi Θεογονία potius quàm Antiphani in Theologiam sacrosanctam ab isto nebulone traductæ sunt, & nominibus Pythagoricorum numerorum dyadis & octoadis venditatæ. Sic igitur Hesiodus, & longè quidem, quàm Valentinus, melius, vt ait Iren. lib. 2. cap. 19.
Ἐ[?]χάος δ' Ἐρέβος τε, μέλαινα τε Νὺξ ἐγένοντο. Νυκτὸς δ' αὖ Αἰθήρ τε καὶ Ἡμέρη ἐξεγένοντο, ὧς τίκτε κυοφορηθεῖσα Ἐρέβει φιλότητι μιγεῖσα,&c.
Ergo Valentinus [?]πλήρωμα quodam ex triginta AEonibus fecit, in quo prima octoas, ex qua cæteri AEones nati sunt, fuit per quatuor [?]ζυγίας siue copulationes, coiens mas AEon cum fœmina.

page.notes: The Greek lines are from Hesiod, Theogony 123–125; the printed forms were copied from the scan and the uncertain letters are marked [?]. The "1" before "Continet" and the "2" before "Triginta" are printed paragraph marks. The small mark under "fœmina" is not a readable note. The page number and running head are small and slightly blurred. Show-through of the facing page lies below the text and was left out.
